settings.title: YAHLA
settings.intro: Alerts when a device that you have not approved joins the network.
settings.statusLine: Listening: __listening__. Packets: __packets__, client events: __events__, unknown: __unknown__, forged: __bad__, from other senders: __foreign__. Devices: __fresh__ new, __approved__ approved, __ignored__ ignored.
settings.warnNoSenders: No sender set: logs from any address are accepted.
settings.deviceLine: Calls itself __name__. IP __ip__, network __network__, at __where__, last seen __last__
settings.sendersHelp: IPv4 addresses that may send logs, separated by commas (at most 5). Senders seen lately are listed below.
settings.networksHelp: Silent = devices are listed but never alerted, for example a guest network.

settings.pinHelp: A PIN is optional. In our tests Homey keeps guests and regular users away from this page's functions. A PIN adds a lock for everyone else who can manage apps on your Homey: the page then asks for it when opened and stays unlocked for 15 minutes after it was last used.
settings.removePinConfirm: Remove the PIN? Then anyone who can open this page can approve devices and change settings.
settings.removePinAgain: Press again within 10 seconds to remove the PIN
settings.logHelp: How much YAHLA writes to the Homey timeline. Serious alarms always come. Flows always get everything.

log.debug: Debug: also your changes, unknown packets and more

sources.title: Which routers work?
sources.intro: YAHLA reads logs that your router sends to Homey (syslog over UDP, port 5514). Enter the router's address under Allowed senders.
sources.unifi: UniFi (UniFi Network, the Activity Logging / SIEM server setting): MAC address, IP address, name, network and VLAN, and which access point or switch port. Tested with real equipment.
sources.asus: ASUS (Asuswrt and Merlin, the Remote log server field): should work. MAC address, IP address, name, network interface (for example br0) and radio (for example eth2). No VLAN. Not yet tested with real equipment.
sources.openwrt: OpenWrt and other routers that log with hostapd and dnsmasq: should work, with the same details as ASUS. Not yet tested with real equipment.
sources.other: Other routers: the router must be able to send syslog to another device. Log lines YAHLA does not understand are counted and reported, never guessed.
sources.note: Good to know: an alert waits up to 10 seconds for the router's DHCP line, so the name and IP address are included. A device with a fixed IP address is only seen through the Wi-Fi line, without name and IP. The name is chosen by the device and can be false; YAHLA recognises a device by its MAC address.

settings.deviceHelp: Approve: never alerts. Ignore: never alerts, shown as ignored. Forget: removed from the list, alerts as new if it is seen again. Remove approval: moves back to new devices.
settings.privateHelp: Phones and watches often use a private address that is different for each network. If such a device changes its address, YAHLA sees it as a new device. In the device's Wi-Fi settings for your home network you can choose a fixed address.
settings.reportHelp: Once a day YAHLA writes to the timeline, so you know it is alive. It is the app's heartbeat: if it does not come, YAHLA is not working. The Flow card for the daily report always runs, also when the report is off.

alarm.silence: **YAHLA has received no logs for __minutes__ minutes.** Check the log sender and the network. Devices are not being checked.
alarm.flood: **Possible flood of network events**: __fresh__ new devices and __events__ client events in 10 minutes. Someone may be faking events.
alarm.floodCap: **Too many device alerts**: more than __capped__ in 10 minutes. Further alerts are only counted. Someone may be faking events.
alarm.unknown: **YAHLA received a log in an unknown format.** It was ignored. If this repeats, check the log sender.
alarm.forged: **YAHLA received a forged or unreadable client event** (repeated identity or no MAC). A device may be trying to hide.
alarm.tamper: **YAHLA setting changed from outside** (__key__). The change was undone. Check who has access to your Homey.
alarm.socket: **YAHLA cannot listen for logs** (__code__). No devices are being checked.
alarm.storeProblem: **YAHLA could not read what it had saved: __what__** (__problem__). It started with defaults.

report.ok: **YAHLA is running.** Since __since__: __packets__ log lines, __newDevices__ new devices.
report.problem: **YAHLA is running but gets no logs.** Last log: __last__. Check the router's log setting.
report.noSocket: **YAHLA cannot listen for logs.** UDP port 5514 on the Homey is not free. YAHLA tries again every minute; see the timeline.
report.unreadable: **YAHLA gets logs but cannot read them.** Since __since__: __packets__ log lines, __unknown__ in a format YAHLA does not know, no device events. No device is checked; see the supported routers in the manual.
report.devices: Devices: __fresh__ waiting for approval, __approved__ approved, __ignored__ ignored.
report.suppressed: Alerts held back because too many came at once: __suppressed__.
report.foreign: Log lines from senders that are not allowed: __foreign__.
